notes: The design system is a constraint system: this file is the machine-readable half of the composition contract. layout-system.md is the prose half; where they disagree the ADR wins.

Detection is property/context-aware, never a blanket text scan: a hex literal in a test fixture, a data file or an icon path table is not a violation. Only color-valued properties inside style objects (css({}), style props, cva variants) and the JSX patterns named per clause are inspected.
Every allowlist entry carries a reason. An entry that waives nothing fails. Growing an allowlist is a contract change reviewed like code; shrinking it is the migration tickets' job (#1109).

scope.exemptNote: src/editorial/** is the DEFINITION side of the contract (tokens, primitives, nav, pet). The gate inspects consumers. Individual files under editorial may still be allowlisted for C-2 when they legitimately carry raw values (icon assets).

notes: Names are the L1/L2 vocabulary of layout-system.md §1. #1106 implements them; until a primitive exists its clause is enforced against the allowlist, not against the missing import.
SectionHeading is an L2 component that internally uses the split grid rule; it is NOT a Grid consumer violation.

C-1.name: section-surface-owner
C-1.summary: Section-level rhythm, page background and section separators belong to PageSection alone.

jsxPatterns.note: a raw <section> outside editorial must be a PageSection or an allowlisted page-composition file

valueRules.note: bg.canvas on a section-scale element is a page-background decision
painting the page ground by hand
section separators are PageSection's borderTop prop

C-1.rationale: Without this clause every section re-decides the page's vertical rhythm, which is how the current HOME became a stack of unrelated beats.

C-2.name: semantic-color-only
C-2.summary: Color-valued properties resolve to semantic tokens only.
C-2.rationale: Raw palette references and literals bypass the semantic layer, so a palette change ripples through feature code and per-component color decisions drift (the current accent-color-on-some-cards failure mode).

C-3.name: section-tone-owner
C-3.summary: Colored/shaded section bands are expressed only through PageSection tone.

detection.sectionScaleHeuristic: a style object containing both a band surface property AND (paddingBlock* OR minHeight OR width:'100%' with block padding) is section-scale and must use PageSection tone
detection.panelPath: smaller classified surfaces use Panel variant="field.*"; arbitrary backgroundColor on a non-allowlisted element is a violation

C-3.rationale: Color must carry section-level meaning (classification or emphasis), assigned by the composition contract — not invented per component. Decorative color is a review failure even when undetectable statically (layout-system.md §4.2).

C-4.name: grid-presets-only
C-4.summary: Grid track definitions live in editorial layout primitives or the page-composition allowlist.
C-4.rationale: Every bespoke grid is a competing coordinate system. The measured 4/8 + container contract only holds if feature code cannot invent tracks.

C-5.name: list-primitive-required
C-5.summary: Repeated rows/lists use RecordList/RecordRow, Grid+Panel or Stack; no per-item boxes.

jsxPatterns.note: a boxed <li> draws a redundant container the section already frames
list layout goes through Stack/Grid presets; listStyle:'none' resets stay allowed

C-5.rationale: layout-system.md §4 (proximity, not boxes) and C-8 (bounded lists) both depend on lists being composed, not decorated per item.

C-6.name: control-primitives-required
C-6.summary: Button/link affordances use Button/TextLink variants; hand-styled lookalikes are forbidden.

jsxPatterns.note: an <a>/<button> styled as a control must be Button/TextLink or an allowlisted non-control (semantic row, tab, resize handle, swatch, editor surface)

C-6.rationale: T3 Code's no-restyle rule: the same look needed twice is a variant on the primitive, not a third hand-rolled copy.

C-7.name: no-duplicate-styling
C-7.summary: The same normalized css({...}) literal in 3+ files is a missing primitive.

detection.method: normalize each css()/cva style object literal (sort keys, drop whitespace), hash it, group by hash across files; report hashes seen in >= minFiles files
detection.exemptNote: single-property resets (margin:0, padding:0, listStyle:none) below minProperties are ignored

C-7.rationale: Duplication is the observable symptom of a missing abstraction; three copies is the promotion threshold (token-audit evidence rule).

C-8.name: curated-pages-enumerate-on-index
C-8.summary: Public pages bound mapped collections; full sets live on dedicated index routes.

jsxPatterns.note: a data collection rendered on a public page must bound the render or link to the index route that owns the enumeration

C-8.rationale: HOME became a long list because every section mapped its whole collection. The full set must remain reachable — on the route whose obligation IS enumeration.

notes: Known-debt entries land here as the #1107 gate inventories current violations; migration tickets (#1108/#1109) shrink them. An allowlist entry is { path, clause, reason } and must still match a live violation.
colorAllowlist: files allowed raw color values (brand marks, icon assets, ad creatives).
gridAllowlist: files allowed bespoke gridTemplate* (page-composition files only, with reason).
sectionAllowlist: files allowed section-level properties outside PageSection (page chrome: masthead/footer/skip-link owned by editorial or composer).
controlAllowlist: elements intentionally not Button/TextLink (semantic rows, tabs, resize handles, swatches, editor surfaces).
listAllowlist: files allowed <li> boxes or unstyled list layout pending migration.
enumerationAllowlist: page files allowed unbounded .map pending the /now + index-route migration (#1108).
